sentences.text: Sinovenator is a genus of troodontid dinosaur from China, a group of small, graceful maniraptorans that closely resemble birds.
All members of this group share unique skull features, such as teeth that are closely packed together in the lower jaw.
A distinguishing feature of Sinovenator is that the front edge of the antorbital fenestra — an opening in the skull — is straight and vertically oriented.
This species is considered one of the larger troodontid species within the ecosystem of the Yixian Formation.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated that a Sinovenator individual one meter long weighed 2.5 kilograms, making it one of the largest troodontid species in its ecosystem.
Fossils of this dinosaur are notable for being preserved in three dimensions rather than being strongly compressed on a slab.
Hundreds of undescribed Sinovenator fossils are known from the Lujiatun Beds, suggesting the species was common in that area.
Two specimens of a troodontid were described in 2002 by Xu Xing, Mark Norell, and colleagues, who found they represented a new taxon named Sinovenator changii.
The generic name means 'Chinese hunter', combining the Latin word for China and the Latin word for hunter, while the species name honors Meemann Chang for her work on the Jehol Fauna.
The holotype specimen, which is the specimen the species is based on, is cataloged as IVPP V 12615 and consists of a partial skull and a disarticulated skeleton.
As troodontids, Sinovenator possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and high encephalization quotients, suggesting advanced behavior and keen senses.
The lack of a bulla on the underside of the braincase is a basal character of Sinovenator.
Sinovenator was classified in the family Troodontidae in 2002.
A 2017 study by Shen et al. placed Sinovenator in a monophyletic group called Sinovenatorinae with other Yixian Formation troodontids.
However, a 2018 study by Yin et al. suggested that Chinese troodontids, including Sinovenator, form an intermediate grade rather than a distinct subfamily.
Sinovenator is a basal or 'primitive' troodontid that shares characteristics with most dromaeosaurids and basal Avialae.
Sinovenator lived during the Early Cretaceous Period, approximately 125 million years ago during the Aptian stage, though more precise dating places it between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
Fossils of Sinovenator were found in the oldest section of the Yixian Formation in China.
Four fossil occurrences of Sinovenator have been recorded.

There was a debate regarding the age of Sinovenator fossils, originally thought to be Hauterivian but later research indicated they are younger. Originally, the basal position of Sinovenator seemed corroborated by a very old age, assuming the fossils dated to the Hauterivian. However, subsequent research indicated that the layers were younger.
It was found that a wide and flattened fourth metatarsal was a synapomorphy uniting this group.
